chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Kurr of water is one thousand two hundred Ratls.

key_terms.الكُرّ: Kurr: a unit of volume in Islamic law; a large body of water that cannot be rendered impure
key_terms.رِطْل: Ratl: a unit of weight (approximately 400 grams in the Iraqi system), used to measure the Kurr

ai.seo_question: What is the volume of the Kurr according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the Kurr — a specific volume measure used in Islamic law — as being equal to 1,200 Ratls (a unit of weight approximately 400 grams each, yielding approximately 480 kg). This legal ruling is foundational in the jurisprudence of ritual purity: a body of water reaching the volume of a Kurr cannot be made ritually impure (najis) by contact with impure substances. This standard was particularly important for water stored in cisterns, wells, or pools used for ritual washing (wudu and ghusl) in the early Islamic community.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Kurr from the water is of (the weight of) one thousand two hundred Ratls (one Ratl = approximately 400 gms)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of our people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
the quantity of one Kur of water is one thousand and two hundred ritl (a certain measurement).”
